name: LMV321IDBVR
title: LMV321, LMV358, LMV324, LMV324S: low-voltage operational amplifiers with rail-to-rail outputs
summary: Single, dual and quad bipolar op amps for 2.7 V to 5.5 V, with outputs that reach close to both rails and an input range that includes ground. Typical bandwidth is 1 MHz at unity gain and the output slews at 1 V/μs; typical supply current at 5 V is 130 μA for the LMV321 and 410 μA for the four amplifiers of the LMV324. The LMV324S adds two shutdown pins, each turning off a pair of amplifiers. LMV321IDBVR is the single LMV321 in the 5-pin SOT-23 (DBV), -40°C to 125°C, on a 3000-piece reel.

circuits.title: Single-ended input to differential output on 2.7 V
circuits.description: Both halves of an LMV358 on one 2.7 V rail turn a 0.5 V to 2 V single-ended signal into a differential pair. Amplifier 1 follows VIN and is VOUT+. Amplifier 2 inverts VOUT+ through R1 and R2, while R3 and R4 halve the 2.5 V reference onto its non-inverting input, so VOUT- = VREF - VIN with all four resistors equal. Each output moves between 0.5 V and 2 V, VDIFF spans ±1.5 V and the common-mode level is VREF/2.
notes: Resistors of 6 kΩ or less keep the resistor noise below the amplifier noise where noise matters.
Signals must stay below the 1 MHz bandwidth.

circuits.title: Non-inverting amplifier
circuits.description: One amplifier as a non-inverting stage: VIN reaches the non-inverting input through RIN, RF feeds the output back to the inverting input and RG ties that input to ground. Each supply pin has a low-ESR 0.1 μF ceramic capacitor to ground; the one on VS- is fitted only for split supplies.

circuits.title: Capacitive-load stability test, unity gain
circuits.description: The amplifier as a follower on ±2.5 V supplies, its output tied back to the inverting input and loaded by RL and CL to ground; a pulse at VI swings the output 100 mVPP, and CL is raised until the overshoot reaches 25 %.

circuits.title: Capacitive-load stability test, gain of 10
circuits.description: The same test at a non-inverting gain of 10: 1.21 MΩ from the output to the inverting input and 134 kΩ from that input to ground, with RL and CL on the output and ±2.5 V supplies.

equations.name: Inverted output
equations.expr: VOUT- = VREF × (R4 / (R3 + R4)) × (1 + R2 / R1) - VIN × R2 / R1

where.R4: lower resistor of the reference divider

equations.name: Differential output
equations.expr: VDIFF = VOUT+ - VOUT- = VIN × (1 + R2 / R1) - VREF × (R4 / (R3 + R4)) × (1 + R2 / R1)

equations.note: The largest input equals VREF, each output reaches at most VREF, and VDIFF spans 2 × VREF.

operation.text: Single (LMV321), dual (LMV358) and quad (LMV324, LMV324S) op amps for 2.7 V to 5.5 V supplies, with rail-to-rail outputs and an input common-mode range that includes ground. Their specifications meet or exceed those of the LM358 and LM324, which run from 5 V to 30 V. Unity-gain bandwidth is 1 MHz and slew rate 1 V/μs; there is no crossover distortion.
Typical supply current: 130 μA for the LMV321, 210 μA for the LMV358, 410 μA for the LMV324 and LMV324S.

Specified and guaranteed from 2.7 V to 5 V, with many limits holding from -40°C to 125°C. Each part runs from a single supply or from split supplies. Above 5.5 V on the supply the part can be damaged permanently.

The LMV324S is an LMV324 with shutdown. Amplifiers 1 and 2 share the 1/2 SHDN pin, amplifiers 3 and 4 the 3/4 SHDN pin; a low level shuts the pair down and a high level runs it. Shut down, each channel draws at most 5 μA and its output is actively pulled low. Turn-on takes about 2 μs and turn-off about 40 ns. The other parts run whenever supply is applied.
A control input that is not used is held at VCC or GND, and VIH is kept no higher than VCC.
One output may be shorted to ground indefinitely at or below 25°C with VCC up to 5.5 V. A short from an output to VCC can heat the part until it fails.

The input is a bipolar differential pair fed from a current source, with diodes from each input to VCC and to ground. The output stage drives the output pin through a series resistor, with diodes from the output to VCC and to ground, and its loop is compensated by a capacitor in series with a resistor.
The LMV321 is also offered in a package about half the size of the 5-pin SOT-23 (DBV).
A 0.1 μF low-ESR ceramic capacitor goes from each supply pin to ground, as close to the part as possible; on a single supply, one capacitor on V+ is enough.

Each supply pin gets a low-ESR 0.1 μF ceramic capacitor to ground, placed close to the part; a single-supply design needs only the one on V+. Analog and digital grounds are kept separate, with a ground plane on one or more inner layers. Input traces run short and away from supply and output traces, crossing them at right angles where they must cross. External parts sit close to the part, with RF and RG next to the inverting input. A low-impedance driven guard ring around critical traces cuts leakage from traces at other potentials.

Targets: 2.7 V supply, 2.5 V reference, 0.5 V to 2 V input, ±1.5 V differential output, with the output range held narrow for linearity. Linearity is set by the input common-mode range and output swing, so both the inputs and the output of the amplifier need to reach the rails; with the 1 MHz bandwidth of the LMV358 the circuit handles signals below 1 MHz. VOUT- depends directly on R1 to R4, so low-tolerance resistors are used; the circuit was built with 36 kΩ resistors measured within 2 %.
Measured with the input swept from 0 V to 2.5 V; the circuit is intended for 0.5 V to 2 V, its most linear range.

Built-in ESD protection is limited: store and handle the part with its leads shorted together or in conductive foam. ESD ratings: 2000 V HBM and 1000 V CDM (exceeds JESD 22); 2500 V HBM and 1500 V CDM on all pins.
